text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Agriculture minister Helmut Angula called for the introduction of a two-year compulsory army service arguing that young Namibians lack national identity.
- Malaria victims in Namibia almost doubled last year with over 400 deaths reported countrywide, compared to 1995 when 207 people died from the disease.
- Final negotiations are underway between the Namibian government and Australian mining company Great Fitzroy Mines aimed at establishing the seventh largest cathode copper mine in the world.
- Namibian women's groups are demanding urgent attention to be given to the Abortion and Sterilisation Bill warning that more women are resorting to backstreet abortions.
